## Guided Tutorial A.1: Securing the Reporting Package

**Context and objective.** In this tutorial, you will review and test the access the controller plans for Charles River Reports. You will start with an access review in internal audit's monitoring file, comparing the managers recorded for each cost center with the employee records. Then you will add a security table and a dynamic role to the package, test the role as several managers would see it, and write internal audit's findings. Internal auditors do not build the controls they audit, so in practice the controller's staff adds the roles and internal audit tests them; in this tutorial you take both parts in turn. Everything in it is done in Power BI Desktop, with no license.

**Prerequisites.** You need Audit Monitoring.pbix from Chapter 16 and Charles River Reports.pbix as you left it at the end of Chapter 15.

**Step-by-step instructions.**

**Step 1. Review the managers of record.**

a. In Audit Monitoring.pbix, choose **Home > Get data > Excel workbook**, select **T75_CostCenter**, click **Transform Data**, and rename the query `CostCenterReview`.
b. Keep CostCenterID, CostCenterName, and ManagerID.
c. Merge it with **Employee** on ManagerID and EmployeeID, and expand EmployeeName, JobTitle, EmploymentStatus, and TerminationDate without the prefix.
d. Choose **Home > Close & Apply**, and add a page named `Access Review` with a table visual of the merged columns.

@fig-a-02 shows the review. Three of the ten cost centers name a terminated employee as their manager, none of whom held a manager's job, and the department managers who now run two of them are not named anywhere. A fourth cost center names an analyst. Access built on this column would go to the wrong people, so the package needs a list of its own.

![The Access Review.](/visuals/svg/fig-a-02-access-review.svg){#fig-a-02 fig-alt="A mock of a Power BI table visual on a page named Access Review. Each row is a cost center with its manager of record, that person's job title, employment status, and termination date. Three rows, for Executive, Sales, and Warehouse, are outlined: their managers of record are terminated employees whose job titles are not managerial. The Research and Development row names an analyst. A note lists the Sales Manager and the Warehouse Manager, who appear in the employee records but not as managers of record."}

**Step 2. Give each employee a cost center in the package.**

a. Open Charles River Reports.pbix, choose **Home > Transform data**, and select the **Employee** query.
b. Choose **Home > Choose Columns**, add CostCenterID, and choose **Home > Close & Apply**.

The Plant page's labor time is related to Employee, so a rule on the employee's cost center can reach it.

**Step 3. Build the security table.**

a. Choose **Home > Enter data**, and in the **Create Table** dialog name two columns `UserPrincipalName` and `CostCenterID`.
b. Type the nine rows of @tbl-a-02, leaving out its Cost center column, which is there for you to read.
c. Type `Security` as the table's name, and click **Load**.
d. In **Model view**, right-click **Security**, and choose **Hide in report view**.

| UserPrincipalName | CostCenterID | Cost center |
|--------------------------------------|------|----------------|
| `employee001@charlesriver.example` | 1 | Executive |
| `employee006@charlesriver.example` | 2 | Sales |
| `employee007@charlesriver.example` | 3 | Warehouse |
| `employee004@charlesriver.example` | 4 | Manufacturing |
| `employee010@charlesriver.example` | 5 | Purchasing |
| `employee005@charlesriver.example` | 6 | Administration |
| `employee011@charlesriver.example` | 7 | Customer Service |
| `employee012@charlesriver.example` | 9 | Marketing |
| `employee014@charlesriver.example` | 10 | Design Services |

: The security table, as approved by the controller {#tbl-a-02}

The table is not related to anything: the rules of the next steps read it.

**Step 4. Check the list against the access review.**

a. Compare each address with the Email column of T74_Employee, which serves here as each user's sign-in name, and with the Access Review page of Step 1.
b. Confirm that each address belongs to the manager the controller named for that cost center.
c. Record the cost center the list leaves out.
d. Record who maintained the list and who approved it.

The list names the managers who actually run each department, as the controller confirmed them, and each of them belongs to the cost center the list gives them. Research and Development is left out until the controller names its manager, so for now no one sees it. The list was prepared by the controller's staff and approved by the controller, so no one both grants and authorizes access, and your check in this step is internal audit's review of it.

**Step 5. Create the role and its first two rules.**

a. Choose **Modeling > Manage roles**, click **New role**, and name the role `Cost Center Managers`.
b. Under **Tables**, select **CostCenter**, click **Switch to DAX editor**, and enter the first rule below.
c. Select **Employee**, and enter the same rule.

<!-- dax-check: skip -->
```
[CostCenterID] IN CALCULATETABLE (
    VALUES ( Security[CostCenterID] ),
    Security[UserPrincipalName] = USERPRINCIPALNAME ()
)
```

The rule keeps a cost center if it is among the cost centers the security table lists for the person viewing the report. On CostCenter it filters the ledger and the budget lines; on Employee it filters the labor time of the Plant page to the employees of those cost centers. @fig-a-03 shows the editor with the rule on CostCenter; the tables that carry a rule are marked in the list.

![The Manage Security Roles Dialog.](/visuals/svg/fig-a-03-manage-roles.svg){#fig-a-03 fig-alt="A mock of Power BI's Manage security roles dialog. The Roles list holds Cost Center Managers and Finance, with a New role button. The Tables list marks CostCenter, Employee, Item, and Security as having a filter. The rules area, switched to the DAX editor, shows the rule on CostCenter, which keeps the cost centers listed in the Security table for the user principal name of the viewer. Save and Close buttons sit at the bottom."}

**Step 6. Deny everyone else, and add a role for finance.**

a. Select **Item**, and enter the first rule below.
b. Select **Security**, and enter the second rule below.
c. Click **New role**, name it `Finance`, and leave it without rules.
d. Click **Save**.

<!-- dax-check: skip -->
```
USERPRINCIPALNAME () IN VALUES ( Security[UserPrincipalName] )
```

<!-- dax-check: skip -->
```
[UserPrincipalName] = USERPRINCIPALNAME ()
```

The invoice lines and the completions are not related to CostCenter, so without the Item rule anyone in the role would see every sale. The rule returns true for every item when the viewer is in the security table and false when the viewer is not, so a person added to the role by mistake sees no sales and no cost centers at all. The rule on Security keeps each user from reading the other users' rows. The Finance role, for the controller and her staff, filters nothing.

**Step 7. View the report as the Sales Manager.**

a. Choose **Modeling > View as**.
b. Select **Other user**, type `employee006@charlesriver.example`, and select **Cost Center Managers**.
c. Click **OK**, and open the Budget page, the Income Statement page, the Plant page, and the Sales and Discounts page in turn.

A bar above the page names the role and the user while you view as them. The Budget page now holds one row, Sales, with the same budget, actual, and flexed budget as before, because the commission budget and the revenue budget it is flexed with both sit in the Sales cost center. The Plant page is empty. The Sales and Discounts page shows every sale, as the controller intends for listed managers. The Income Statement shows a net income more than twice the company's, because it sets Sales' revenue against Sales' costs only, and nothing on the page says so.

**Step 8. View the report as three more people.**

a. Repeat Step 7 for `employee007@charlesriver.example`, the Warehouse Manager.
b. Record what the Budget and Income Statement pages show.
c. Repeat Step 7 for `employee004@charlesriver.example`, the Production Manager.
d. Record what the Budget and Plant pages show.
e. Repeat Step 7 for `employee083@charlesriver.example`, the terminated employee recorded as manager of Sales.
f. Choose **Stop viewing** to return to your own view.

The Warehouse Manager sees the Warehouse budget and an income statement that is a loss. The Production Manager sees the whole Plant page but an empty Budget page, because Manufacturing's costs are budgeted as cost of goods sold, not operating expense, so the page meant for department managers does not serve this one. The former employee, absent from the security table, sees nothing at all, which is the deny-by-default design working.

**Step 9. Tell readers what they are seeing.**

a. Add the two measures below to the Measures table.
b. Add a card of Cost Centers Shown to the Budget page and the Income Statement page, titled `Cost centers shown`.
c. Add a card of Who Am I to the About page.

<!-- dax-check: measure -->
```
Cost Centers Shown =
CONCATENATEX (
    DISTINCT ( CostCenter[CostCenterName] ),
    CostCenter[CostCenterName], ", ",
    CostCenter[CostCenterName], ASC
)
```

<!-- dax-check: measure -->
```
Who Am I = USERPRINCIPALNAME ()
```

DISTINCT leaves out the blank row that the ledger lines without a cost center would add to VALUES. Who Am I shows the name the rules compare. In the service it is the reader's sign-in name, and in View as it is the user you typed. In Desktop without View as it is your own Windows sign-in, which on a computer without a work account reads as the computer's name and yours; no rule applies to you there, because roles take effect only for readers.

**Step 10. Check the cards as two managers.**

a. View the Budget page as the Sales Manager, as in Step 7.
b. View the Income Statement page as the Warehouse Manager.
c. Choose **Stop viewing**, and look at both pages again.

Viewed as a manager, the card names that manager's cost centers, the only sign on the page that its totals are partial, as @fig-a-04 shows; without a role, it lists them all. A reader who sees an unexpected name, or none of the expected cost centers, knows to ask before relying on the page.

![The Package Viewed as Two Managers.](/visuals/svg/fig-a-04-view-as.svg){#fig-a-04 fig-alt="Two mocks of report pages viewed through View as, each with a bar at the top naming the role Cost Center Managers and the user. On the left, the Budget page viewed as the Sales Manager shows a single row for Sales and a card reading Cost centers shown: Sales. On the right, the Income Statement viewed as the Warehouse Manager shows only Warehouse expenses and a net loss, with a card reading Cost centers shown: Warehouse, the only sign on the page that the statement is partial."}

**Step 11. Write the findings.** Write a short memo from internal audit to the controller that sets out what the review found and what you recommend.

a. Describe the managers of record and why the role does not use them.
b. Recommend who maintains the security table, who approves it, and how often internal audit reviews it.
c. Describe what each manager sees, including the pages that become partial and the Budget page that does not serve the Production Manager.
d. Save both files.

**Checkpoint.** Before you report to the controller, confirm the following:

- The access review lists the managers of record against the employee records, with the terminated managers visible.
- Viewed as the Sales Manager, the Budget page shows only Sales, and the card says so.
- Viewed as the terminated manager of record, the report shows nothing.
- Your memo names the pages that a role leaves partial and who maintains, approves, and reviews the security table.

Row-level security is only as good as the list behind it and the pages it is applied to, and both are things an auditor can test before any manager opens the report.
